title: John Chapter 7 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on John chapter 7 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: John Chapter 7 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of John Chapter 7.

questions.question: Why did Jesus walk in Galilee instead of Jewry?
options: Because he sought to teach in secret
Because the Jews sought to kill him
Because he was with his disciples
questions.correctAnswer: Because the Jews sought to kill him
questions.explanation: Jesus walked in Galilee because the Jews sought to kill him, as stated in John 7:1.

questions.question: What feast was near at hand in John 7?
questions.explanation: The text mentions that the Jews' feast of tabernacles was at hand in John 7:2.

questions.question: What did Jesus' brethren suggest he do?
questions.explanation: His brethren suggested he depart and go into Judaea so that his disciples may see his works, as stated in John 7:3.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus' brethren believed in him.
questions.explanation: The text states that neither did his brethren believe in him, as indicated in John 7:5.

questions.question: What did Jesus say about his time?
questions.explanation: Jesus indicated that his time was not yet come, as stated in John 7:6.

questions.question: True or False: The world cannot hate Jesus' brethren.
questions.explanation: Jesus stated that the world cannot hate his brethren, but it hateth him, as noted in John 7:7.

questions.question: Where did Jesus go after his brethren went to the feast?
questions.explanation: Jesus remained in Galilee until after his brethren had left, as noted in John 7:9.

questions.question: How did Jesus go up to the feast?
questions.explanation: Jesus went up to the feast not openly, but as it were in secret, as stated in John 7:10.

questions.question: True or False: Many people spoke openly about Jesus at the feast due to fear of the Jews.
questions.explanation: The text states that no man spake openly of him for fear of the Jews, as indicated in John 7:13.

questions.question: What did the Jews marvel about Jesus?
questions.explanation: The Jews marveled at how Jesus knew letters, having never learned, as stated in John 7:15.

questions.question: In John 7:16, whose doctrine did Jesus claim it was?
questions.explanation: Jesus asserted that his doctrine was not his own, but that of him who sent him, which refers to his father, as stated in John 7:16.

questions.question: Did Moses give the law according to Jesus?
questions.explanation: Jesus asked if Moses did not give the law, indicating that he acknowledged Moses as the giver of the law, as stated in John 7:19.

questions.question: What does Jesus say will happen if a man does God's will?
questions.explanation: Jesus stated that if any man will do his will, he shall know of the doctrine, as mentioned in John 7:17.

questions.question: True or False: The people believed that Jesus was a good man.
questions.explanation: Some said Jesus is a good man, as noted in John 7:12.

questions.question: In what manner did Jesus teach during the feast?
questions.explanation: The people remarked that Jesus spoke boldly, as noted in John 7:26.

medium.title: John Chapter 7 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from John Chapter 7 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Why did Jesus choose not to walk in Jewry according to John 7?
options: Because the Jews sought to kill him
questions.correctAnswer: Because the Jews sought to kill him
questions.explanation: Jesus did not walk in Jewry because the Jews sought to kill him, as stated in John 7:1.

questions.question: What did Jesus' brethren encourage him to do in John 7?
questions.explanation: His brethren told him to depart and go into Judaea so his disciples could see his works, as mentioned in John 7:3.

questions.question: According to John 7:5, how did Jesus' brethren view him?
questions.explanation: The scripture notes that neither did his brethren believe in him, indicating skepticism, as stated in John 7:5.

questions.question: What does John 7:24 teach about judging others?
questions.explanation: Jesus instructed to judge not according to appearance but to judge righteous judgment in John 7:24.

questions.question: What did Jesus claim about his doctrine in John 7:16?
options: It is from the Father who sent him
questions.correctAnswer: It is from the Father who sent him
questions.explanation: Jesus stated that his doctrine is not his own, but from the one who sent him, highlighting its divine origin in John 7:16.

questions.question: True or False: The people openly spoke about Jesus without fear of the Jews in John 7:13.
questions.explanation: No man spoke openly of Jesus for fear of the Jews, as stated in John 7:13, indicating a climate of fear.

questions.question: According to John 7:31, what did many of the people believe about Jesus?
questions.explanation: Many believed that Jesus was the Prophet when they heard his teachings as noted in John 7:40.

questions.question: What question did the Jews ask among themselves in John 7:35?
questions.explanation: The Jews wondered where Jesus would go that they could not find him, as expressed in John 7:35.

questions.question: True or False: According to John 7:36, the people understood the meaning of Jesus' statement about seeking him.
questions.explanation: They did not understand what manner of saying this was, indicating confusion about his message in John 7:36.

questions.question: In John 7:29, how does Jesus assert his relationship with the one who sent him?
options: He knows him and is sent by him
questions.correctAnswer: He knows him and is sent by him
questions.explanation: Jesus affirmed that he knows the one who sent him, differentiating himself from the people’s ignorance about God in John 7:29.

questions.question: What does John 7:23 illustrate about the law of Moses and the Sabbath?
options: It is more important than healing
questions.explanation: This verse shows that the law permitted circumcision on the Sabbath, highlighting a priority of human need over strict law observance in John 7:23.

questions.question: What does John 7:30 indicate about the timing of events in Jesus' ministry?
options: He was always in control of the situation
He was confused about his mission
questions.correctAnswer: He was always in control of the situation
questions.explanation: This verse reveals that no one could lay hands on Jesus because his hour had not yet come, indicating divine timing in John 7:30.

questions.question: How does John 7:21 demonstrate Jesus' authority over miracles?
options: He claims he has done no works
He is unsure of his abilities
questions.explanation: Jesus mentions that he has done one work which caused marvel, showing his authority and power as recorded in John 7:21.

hard.title: John Chapter 7 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from John Chapter 7.

questions.question: What did Jesus declare on the last day of the feast?
options: If any man thirst, let him come unto me, and drink.
I am the light of the world.
The kingdom of God is at hand.
Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.
questions.correctAnswer: If any man thirst, let him come unto me, and drink.
questions.explanation: Jesus invited those who were thirsty to come to him and drink (John 7:37), emphasizing the spiritual sustenance he offers.

questions.question: What was the people's reaction to Jesus' declaration about believing in him?
options: They thought he was a false prophet.
They believed he was the Prophet.
questions.correctAnswer: They believed he was the Prophet.
questions.explanation: Many of the people, upon hearing Jesus' words, recognized him as a prophet (John 7:40), reflecting their understanding of his authority.

questions.question: What division arose among the people regarding Jesus?
options: Some believed he was the Messiah.
Some were confused about his origins.
Some wanted to crown him king.
questions.correctAnswer: Some were confused about his origins.
questions.explanation: There was a division among the people, with some questioning if Christ could come from Galilee (John 7:41-43), highlighting their misunderstanding of prophecy.

questions.question: What did the officers say when they did not bring Jesus to the chief priests?
options: Never man spake like this man.
questions.correctAnswer: Never man spake like this man.
questions.explanation: The officers were struck by Jesus' words, stating that no man spoke like him (John 7:46), indicating his unique authority and wisdom.

questions.question: What did Nicodemus question regarding the law?
options: If it is lawful to heal on the Sabbath.
If any man should be judged without hearing him.
If the law is fulfilled in Christ.
If the law allows for circumcision.
questions.correctAnswer: If any man should be judged without hearing him.
questions.explanation: Nicodemus argued that the law requires a man to be heard before judgment (John 7:51), advocating for justice and due process.

questions.question: What does Jesus mean by 'living water' in John 7:38?
questions.explanation: Jesus referred to the 'living water' as the Spirit, indicating the sustenance and life that comes from believing in him (John 7:39).

questions.question: What literary device is demonstrated by the contrasting views of Jesus among the people?
questions.explanation: The contrasting opinions about Jesus' identity illustrate parallelism, showing the divided perspectives of the people (John 7:40-43).

questions.question: How did the Pharisees respond to the crowd's interest in Jesus?
options: They encouraged people to follow him.
They sent officers to arrest him.
questions.correctAnswer: They sent officers to arrest him.
questions.explanation: The Pharisees and chief priests, worried about Jesus' influence, sent officers to take him (John 7:32), showing their desire to control the situation.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus said that the world could not hate his brethren.
questions.explanation: Jesus stated that the world cannot hate his brethren, indicating that he alone faced animosity due to his testimony (John 7:7).

questions.question: True or False: The Jews knew where Jesus came from.
questions.explanation: The people expressed confusion regarding Jesus' origins, stating that they knew where he was from, but when the Christ comes, his origin will be unknown (John 7:27).

questions.question: Which Old Testament prophet is often connected to Jesus' proclamation in John 7:37 about living water?
questions.explanation: Isaiah speaks of the coming Messiah providing living water and spiritual sustenance (Isaiah 55:1), echoing Jesus' declaration in John 7:37.

questions.question: Which Psalm is reflected in the idea of rivers of living water flowing from believers?
questions.explanation: Psalm 46:4 speaks of a river whose streams make glad the city of God, paralleling the 'living water' theme in John 7:38.

questions.question: How does John 7:24 instruct believers regarding judgment?
questions.explanation: Jesus taught not to judge by appearance but to judge with righteousness (John 7:24), emphasizing the need for discernment and fairness.

questions.question: What key Greek word is used in John 7:38 for 'believe', and what does it imply?
questions.explanation: The Greek word 'pisteuo' implies a deep trust in Jesus, crucial for receiving the living water he offers (John 7:38).

questions.question: What did the people expect regarding the Messiah’s origins according to John 7:42?
options: He would be a descendant of the Pharisees.
He would be born in Egypt.
questions.explanation: The scripture indicated that the Messiah would come from the seed of David and from Bethlehem, which the people recognized (John 7:42).

theological.title: John Chapter 7 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from John Chapter 7 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does John 7:7 reveal about the world's attitude towards Jesus?
options: The world is indifferent to Jesus
questions.explanation: John 7:7 states, 'The world cannot hate you; but me it hateth, because I testify of it, that the works thereof are evil.' This indicates that Jesus is hated by the world due to His testimony against it.

questions.question: What did Jesus mean when he said, 'My doctrine is not mine, but his that sent me'?
options: He is teaching his own ideas
He is teaching the ideas of Moses
He is teaching the doctrine of God
He is confused about his teachings
questions.correctAnswer: He is teaching the doctrine of God
questions.explanation: In John 7:16, Jesus clarifies that His teachings originate from God, highlighting His divine authority and the unity of His message with God's will.

questions.question: According to John 7:19, what inconsistency does Jesus point out among the Jews regarding the law of Moses?
options: They do not keep the law
questions.correctAnswer: They do not keep the law
questions.explanation: Jesus challenges them in John 7:19, asking, 'Did not Moses give you the law, and yet none of you keepeth the law?' This reveals their hypocrisy in claiming to uphold the law while plotting to kill Him.

questions.question: What did the people think of Jesus during the feast according to John 7:12?
questions.explanation: John 7:12 records that some people said, 'He is a good man,' while others disagreed, illustrating the divided opinions about Jesus during the feast.

questions.question: What is the primary theme expressed in John 7:38 regarding belief in Jesus?
options: Belief allows one to escape judgment
questions.explanation: John 7:38 states, 'He that believeth on me, as the scripture hath said, out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water.' This metaphor emphasizes the spiritual fulfillment that comes from believing in Jesus.

questions.question: What does John 7:24 teach about judgment?
options: Judgment should be based on appearances
questions.explanation: In John 7:24, Jesus instructs, 'Judge not according to the appearance, but judge righteous judgment.' This highlights the importance of discernment based on truth rather than superficiality.

questions.question: How does Jesus' statement in John 7:34 relate to His eventual departure?
options: He will go to teach others
questions.explanation: In John 7:34, Jesus says, 'Ye shall seek me, and shall not find me: and where I am, thither ye cannot come.' This indicates His impending departure and the spiritual implications of seeking Him after He is gone.

questions.question: What does John 7:30 indicate about the divine timing of Jesus' ministry?
options: Jesus controls the timing of His actions
Jesus is unaware of the timing
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus controls the timing of His actions
questions.explanation: John 7:30 reveals that 'they sought to take him: but no man laid hands on him, because his hour was not yet come.' This emphasizes that Jesus' actions are subject to divine timing.

questions.question: What does the division among the people in John 7:43 signify?
questions.explanation: John 7:43 states, 'So there was a division among the people because of him,' indicating differing beliefs and confusion regarding who Jesus truly is.

questions.question: What doctrine does John 7:39 reveal about the Holy Spirit?
options: The Holy Spirit was given at creation
The Holy Spirit was not yet given
The Holy Spirit is only for the prophets
questions.correctAnswer: The Holy Spirit was not yet given
questions.explanation: John 7:39 notes, '(But this spake he of the Spirit, which they that believe on him should receive: for the Holy Ghost was not yet given; because that Jesus was not yet glorified.)' This teaches that the giving of the Holy Spirit was linked to Jesus' glorification.

questions.question: What does Jesus' teaching in John 7:28 imply about His origin?
questions.explanation: In John 7:28, Jesus claims, 'Ye both know me, and ye know whence I am: and I am not come of myself, but he that sent me is true, whom ye know not.' This asserts His divine origin and mission.

questions.question: What sceptical claim about Jesus does John 7:52 suggest, and how does it contrast with His identity?
options: Jesus is a descendant of David
questions.explanation: John 7:52 reflects the sceptical view that 'Art thou also of Galilee? Search, and look: for out of Galilee ariseth no prophet.' This contrasts with the truth of Jesus' prophetic and messianic identity.

questions.question: What do John 7:3-4 combined teach about the expectations of Jesus' brethren?
options: They wanted Him to show off
They desired Him to remain hidden
questions.correctAnswer: They wanted Him to show off
questions.explanation: John 7:3-4 shows that Jesus' brethren urged Him to go to Judea to display His works, revealing their misunderstanding of His mission and the nature of His ministry.

questions.question: What doctrinal insight can be drawn from John 7:14-15 regarding Jesus' teaching?
options: He teaches from the law of Moses
questions.explanation: In John 7:14-15, Jesus teaches in the temple and astonishes the Jews, indicating that His teaching comes with divine authority, not learned from human sources.

questions.question: What synthesis of doctrine can be observed in John 7:6 and 7:8 regarding Jesus and His timing?
options: Jesus ignores the needs of people
Jesus is confused about His mission
questions.explanation: John 7:6 states that 'My time is not yet come,' and John 7:8 confirms this by showing that Jesus did not go to the feast openly. This synthesis emphasizes the significance of divine timing in Jesus' ministry.
